note.explanation: Distance tells how much actual path an object travels. Displacement tells how far and in what direction it is from its starting position to its final position.
examples: A car may travel 320 km along roads from Lahore to Multan; that is its distance travelled.
If the car’s starting and ending points are A and B, the straight, directed line from A to B represents its displacement.
note.checkAnswer: Distance is the length of the actual path; displacement is the shortest directed distance from the initial position to the final position.
note.simple: Distance is the route taken. Displacement is the straight way from where you started to where you ended, including its direction.
note.checkQuestion: What is the difference between distance and displacement?
note.title: Distance and Displacement
steps: Identify the actual path travelled: its length is the distance.
Identify the initial and final positions.
Join these positions with a straight line and show its direction from initial to final: this is the displacement.
note.answer: Distance is the length of actual path of the motion. Displacement is the shortest distance from the initial to the final position, with direction from the initial position to the final position.

written.text: Distance and displacement may or may not be equal in magnitude. Explain this statement.
written.finalAnswer: Distance and displacement are equal in magnitude when motion is along a straight line in one direction. If the path is curved or the object changes direction, distance is greater than the magnitude of displacement.

examTips: This section is commonly tested by asking for the definitions of distance and displacement or asking you to explain their difference.
In a comparison answer, earn marks by stating that distance is the length of the actual path and displacement is the shortest straight-line separation from the initial to final position.
Remember to include the direction of displacement and the scalar/vector distinction when asked to explain the difference.
For a path diagram, show the actual route for distance and a straight arrow from the initial position to the final position for displacement.

example.question: Suppose a car travels from a position A to B. Identify its distance and displacement.
example.answer: Distance is the length of the curved path AB. Displacement d is the straight line AB directed from A to B.

explain.title: Distance measures the route
explain.body: The distance is the length of actual path of the motion. It is a scalar quantity, so it has magnitude but no direction.

explain.title: Displacement measures the change in position
explain.body: The displacement of an object is a vector quantity whose magnitude is the shortest distance between the initial and final positions of the motion and its direction is from the initial position to the final position.

explain.title: They can have different magnitudes
explain.body: If an object follows a curved path or turns, its actual path is longer than the straight-line displacement. If it travels straight in one direction, the distance and the magnitude of displacement are equal.

explain.title: They have the same SI unit
explain.body: The SI unit for the displacement is the same as that of distance: metre (m).

mistakes: Calling distance a vector or displacement a scalar. Distance is scalar; displacement is vector.
Using the length of a curved route as the displacement. Displacement is the straight-line separation between the initial and final positions.
Leaving out the direction of displacement. State that it points from the initial position to the final position.
Assuming distance and displacement are always equal. They are equal in magnitude only for straight-line motion in one direction.
